title: The descent datum is defined at a finite separable level
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral,
and let $(J_s,\varphi)$ be the scheme with its
descent datum furnished by
[lem-pd-canonical-descent-datum] and [lem-pd-descent-cocycle]. Then
there are a finite separable extension $K/k$, a scheme $J_K$ of finite
presentation over $K$, and a descent datum
$\varphi_K$ on $J_K$ over $\Spec(K)/\Spec(k)$ such that
$J_K\times_KK_s\cong J_s$ and such that $\varphi_K$
base changes to $\varphi$; moreover $J_K$ may
be chosen projective over $K$.

proof.text: Base change the curve to ks and use its geometric degree-zero Picard representation. Its representing scheme Js is smooth, proper and geometrically integral. The existing Picard group law makes it an abelian variety, hence it admits a projective embedding.

Apply finite-presentation spreading to Js, obtaining a finite separable model JK. Apply universal-transport spreading and faithfully flat testing to refine JK to JL carrying the canonical descent datum of Js. The identity and cocycle are checked by epimorphism cancellation, without spreading equality constraints to a later stage.

Descend properness from Js to JL. Descend quasi-projectivity by the existing field-base-change theorem (whose proof uses very-ample descent); properness makes its immersion into projective space closed. Pull back an affine basic open obtained by graded prime avoidance to contain any prescribed finite subset.
